body:
Plan: EX-10 + EX-11.

Problem
Near LAND and a first LOD ring are wired, but exterior continuity is not complete: the roadmap still calls out missing 8/16/32 bands and .btr normals, and there is no cross-game crack/overlap gate.

Acceptance
- Real-data guards cover LAND height, normal, vertex color, splat/material, holes, and collider/render agreement per game.
- Adjacent near cells have no geometric cracks or texture discontinuities.
- Select 4/8/16/32 terrain and object LOD bands with stable hysteresis.
- Wire .btr normal maps and VWD full-model culling.
- Define far-plane/reversed-Z policy for the full exterior scale.
- Automated captures detect near/LOD overlap, double draws, holes, and thrash while crossing boundaries.
- Calibrate on Oblivion Tamriel, FNV WastelandNV, Skyrim Tamriel, and FO4 Commonwealth.

comments.body:
## Partial: buildable slices of EX-11 landed in d96110eb

Two of EX-11's named items were pure-CPU work and are done. The rest of #2371 needs a GPU and on-disk game data, so **this issue stays open**.

### Landed

**4/8/16/32 band selection with hysteresis** — new `cell_loader::lod_bands`. A top-down quadtree descent that *partitions* the ring (each node either draws itself or recurses into its four children, never both), so no-overlap/no-gaps is structural rather than a tuning exercise. Wired into both terrain (`.btr`) and object (`.bto`) LOD; previously both streamed one hardcoded level-4 ring.

Band distances are the games' own `[TerrainManager]` settings read from the shipped `Ultra.ini`, not invented:

| Setting | Skyrim SE | FO4 |
|---|---|---|
| `fBlockLevel0Distance` | 60000 | 60000 |
| `fBlockLevel1Distance` | 90000 | 90000 |
| `fBlockLevel2Distance` | *(absent)* | 110000 |
| `fBlockMaximumDistance` | 250000 | 250000 |

**`.btr` normal maps** — the per-quad tangent-space `_n.dds`, bound through the same `MaterialTextureHandles` component every NIF material uses, refcounted and released on unload.

### Real-data findings worth recording

Measured against the installed games (2026-08-12):

- Baked LOD is an **exact quadtree**: `Skyrim - Meshes1.bsa` ships 2304 / 576 / 144 / 36 `tamriel.<level>.*.btr` at levels 4/8/16/32; `Fallout4 - Meshes.ba2` ships the identical terrain counts for `commonwealth`. Everything above level 4 was dead weight on disk before this.
- **Skyrim's coarsest object band is 16, not 32.** It authors no `fBlockLevel2Distance` *and* ships no level-32 `.bto` (517 / 152 / 48 at 4/8/16). FO4 authors the setting and ships all four. The ladder derives this instead of hardcoding a per-game cap.
- **The band metric must measure to the quad centre, not its nearest cell.** On a nearest-cell metric FO4's level-16 window is five cells wide while level-16 quads step 16 cells at a time, so *no* player position can ever select one — the 144 level-16 `.btr` and 48 level-16 `.bto` would stay orphaned forever. Vanilla's exact measurement point is unverified (no engine source); centre distance is the reading that makes the shipped asset counts consistent with the shipped band distances. **This is the top candidate for the calibration gate below to confirm or correct.**
- **FO4 terrain LOD normals are `_msn` (model-space), Skyrim's are `_n` (tangent-space).** Binding `_msn` into the tangent-space slot would shade worse than no normal map, so FO4 is deliberately left unbound — it needs `MAT_FLAG_MODEL_SPACE_NORMALS`, which only reaches the shader through a `Material` component that LOD entities do not have. **Blocked on #2444.**
- The full-detail boundary annulus is a real, pre-existing gap: a finest-level quad straddling `radius_unload` is dropped whole, so up to `LOD_LEVELS[0] - 1` cells of distant terrain are missing against the streamed region. Now pinned by a test rather than left implicit. Closing it needs VWD full-model culling (below).

### Not addressed — still the substance of EX-10/11

- **EX-10 entirely**: per-game real-data guards for LAND height / normal / vertex colour / splat / holes / collider-render agreement, and adjacent-cell crack + texture-discontinuity checks.
- **VWD full-model culling** — the fix for the boundary annulus above. The `VisibleWhenDistant` marker exists (#1889) but nothing consumes it.
- **`.btr` normal maps for FO4** — blocked on #2444.
- **Far-plane / reversed-Z policy** for the full exterior scale.
- **Automated captures** for near/LOD overlap, double draws, holes, and thrash across boundaries.
- **Calibration on Oblivion Tamriel, FNV WastelandNV, Skyrim Tamriel, FO4 Commonwealth** — including confirming the centre-distance metric.

### Risk note

Oblivion / FO3 / FNV bake no quadtree, so `LodBandLadder::for_game` returns `None` and they keep their existing single synthesized ring untouched — this change is a no-op for them. Skyrim/FO4 genuinely change shape: the level-4 band shrinks from 48 cells to ~15 while 8/16/32 extend reach to ~61 cells. That is the vanilla behaviour and coverage is complete (a missing coarse `.btr` subdivides rather than holing), but the visual result is exactly what the blocked capture gate above would verify and has **not** been checked on a GPU.

Verification: full workspace suite green (1087 passed in `byroredux`). The one failing test, `render::fire_lights::derived_reach_is_currently_oversized`, fails identically on a clean tree — pre-existing and unrelated.

## Far-plane / reversed-Z policy — 9e96a9f9

Follow-up to d96110eb, which surfaced a regression it had itself introduced.

### The regression

The band ladder pushed Skyrim/FO4 distant terrain out to 61 cells = 249 856 BU per axis, a **353 350 BU far-corner diagonal**. `DEFAULT_RENDER_DISTANCE` was still **300 000**, sized for the 48-cell synthesized ring it replaced. Frustum planes are extracted from the view-projection matrix, so the shortfall *culls* rather than clips — whole LOD blocks wink out along the view diagonals.

Fixed by raising the far plane to 400 000 (the corner plus ~13% for terrain relief), and by making the coupling non-droppable: `terrain_lod` pins `MAX_LOD_RING_REACH_CELLS` and const-asserts `far² >= 2·reach²` in exact integer math. Deepening the ring or shortening the far plane now fails the build. I verified the assert fires by rebuilding at the old 300 000 — it does.

### Depth policy, with numbers instead of a TODO

`Camera::depth_resolution_at` reports the world-space span of one depth step for the pipeline's real setup (`D32_SFLOAT`, conventional near→0 mapping). Measured:

| Distance | near=0.1 (current) | near=5.0 (vanilla `fNearDistance`) |
|---|---:|---:|
| 1 000 BU | 0.6 | 0.01 |
| 50 000 BU | 1 490 | 30 |
| 196 608 BU (old ring) | 23 040 | 461 |
| 250 000 BU (new ring) | **37 253** | 745 |

So there is effectively **no depth discrimination between distant terrain and the object LOD standing on it**. Note this was already ~23 000 units at the *old* ring — it is long-standing, not introduced by the band work, and it is a strong candidate explanation for distant LOD z-fighting whenever the capture gate below gets run. The band ladder makes it more visible simply because object LOD now reaches much further.

### Why neither remedy is applied yet

- **Raising the near plane** is what every shipped Gamebryo game does (`fNearDistance` = 5 in `Fallout_default.ini`, 10 in `Oblivion_default.ini`) and buys ~50×. It cannot be a constant edit: one camera contract serves both BU-scale worldspaces and the unit-scale demo/loose-NIF scenes, and `scene.rs` parks the no-content camera 4 units from the origin — a 5-unit near plane would swallow it entirely. **Scale-aware `near` is a real design change**, and is the concrete next step if someone wants the cheap 50×.
- **Reversed-Z** is the actual fix and pairs well with `D32_SFLOAT`, but it touches the projection, depth clear, pipeline compare state, and every depth consumer (SSAO, SVGF reprojection, TAA, composite, water, FSR3 linearization). None of those failure modes are visible to `cargo test`, so it needs the GPU capture gate this issue still owes.

Both are now documented on `DEFAULT_RENDER_DISTANCE` with the measurements, so the follow-up is specified rather than vague.

### Still open on #2371

Unchanged from the previous comment except that the far-plane item is now closed:

- EX-10 entirely (per-game real-data LAND guards, adjacent-cell cracks/discontinuities, collider-render agreement).
- **VWD full-model culling** — I looked at this first as the next slice and backed off: `VisibleWhenDistant`'s own doc states the cull requires decoupling the full-detail radius from the streaming ring, which reintroduces the #1866 overlap risk and explicitly needs real-game visual validation. That is the blocked gate, so implementing it blind would be exactly the wrong move.
- `.btr` normal maps for FO4 (`_msn` model-space) — blocked on #2444.
- Reversed-Z, and scale-aware near plane.
- Automated captures for near/LOD overlap, double draws, holes, thrash.
- Calibration on the four primary worldspaces — including confirming the centre-distance band metric from the previous comment.

Verification: 3 files, scoped to `byroredux` + `byroredux-core`; clippy clean on both; full workspace suite run once as the final gate (79 targets green). The one failure, `render::fire_lights::derived_reach_is_currently_oversized`, is pre-existing and unrelated — it fails identically on a clean tree.

## Automated near/LOD overlap + thrash detection — 235c787c

Follow-up to d96110eb/9e96a9f9. Picks off one item from the "Automated captures for near/LOD overlap, double draws, holes, and thrash" line.

### What landed

A live-residency coverage audit, not a screenshot pixel-diff. `lod_bands::select_lod_quads`'s `partition_*` tests already prove the *desired* quad set has no gaps/overlaps by construction; they can't prove the *live* `HashMap`s a real traversal holds still match that after every load/unload/reconcile/boundary crossing. This checks live state instead of re-deriving the desired set:

- **Overlap** (`cell_loader::lod_coverage::find_overlaps` / `find_full_detail_overlaps`) — AABB checks over the resident quad set, same-scheme and cross-scheme against resident full-detail cells (the boundary this system depends on staying conservative, #1866/#1871).
- **Churn** (`ChurnTracker`) — flags a quad key that left residency and came back. Distinct from `StreamingTelemetry::superseded_lod`, which only catches one in-flight load cancelled by the *next* boundary, not a settled key flapping across several.

New `LodCoverageStats` resource (mirrors `RtIntegrityStats`'s `verdict()`/`machine_line()` shape) and `lod.coverage` console command, wired into `m-exteriors.sh` as a new HARD FAIL gate in `boundary` mode.

"Holes" are deliberately not re-derived — `LodReconcileProgress::complete` already answers that from inside the one place that computes the desired set.

Placement LOD (Oblivion's per-cell `_far.nif` scheme) has no quad-footprint concept and stays out of scope here, same as it's excluded from the band ladder.

### Verified for real, not just unit-tested

Rebuilt the release binary and ran it against installed Skyrim Tamriel (2,-4):

- Static mode: 6374 entities, `lod.coverage` reported 541 resident terrain quads / 716 resident object quads, zero overlaps, verdict=PASS.
- Probed the same held session across sunrise/noon/sunset/night (`time.set` 06:00/12:00/18:00/23:00) — every `lod.coverage` field was identical at all four, confirming LOD coverage correctness is time-of-day invariant (expected: band selection is purely player-position-driven).
- `boundary` mode's full 900-frame `grid-cross` traversal hit a Vulkan `wait_for_fences: device lost` a few hundred frames in — a raw GPU/driver failure inside frame submission, nowhere near this change (CPU-only key-set arithmetic). Not chased further per the standing rule against speculative Vulkan fixes for failures invisible to `cargo test`; flagging in case it recurs for someone with headroom to run RenderDoc.

14 new unit tests. Full workspace suite green.

### Still open on #2371

- EX-10 entirely: per-game real-data LAND guards (height/normal/vertex-colour/splat/holes/collider-render agreement), adjacent-cell crack/texture-discontinuity checks.
- VWD full-model culling beyond today's coarse radius gate (per the previous comment: needs decoupling the full-detail radius from the streaming ring, which reintroduces the #1866 overlap risk — needs the GPU gate to validate blind).
- `.btr` normal maps for FO4 (`_msn` model-space) — blocked on #2444.
- Reversed-Z, and scale-aware near plane.
- Cross-game calibration on Oblivion Tamriel, FNV WastelandNV, Skyrim Tamriel, FO4 Commonwealth — including confirming the centre-distance band metric.
- A working `boundary`/`soak`-mode capture run of the new `lod.coverage` gate itself, blocked on whatever caused the device-lost above.

Landed a VWD-culling slice in 2a84ab97 — **not closing**, the rest of EX-10/11 is still open (see below).

## What landed

Picked "VWD full-model culling" as the next slice after 235c787c's LOD-ring coverage audit. Investigating before writing anything found it's not a one-sitting feature: the VWD / "Has Distant LOD" flag is already fully parsed (#1731) and materialised per placement as the `VisibleWhenDistant` marker (#1889) — with **no render-time consumer today, by design**. Full REFRs only ever spawn inside `radius_unload`, both LOD rings load strictly outside it, so a full model and its `.bto` proxy structurally never coexist. There's nothing to cull yet.

Building the *active* cull means first giving VWD-flagged REFRs their own streaming radius beyond `radius_unload` — today's streaming is whole-cell granularity only, nothing spawns an individual REFR independent of its cell. `exal.md` §5.2 already says that decoupling "needs real-game visual validation before it is enabled," which this session can't provide. Building it anyway and shipping it disabled would be real effort with no way to prove it correct beyond synthetic tests, and enabling it blind is exactly the kind of visually-consequential, `cargo-test`-invisible change this project's standing policy says not to ship speculatively.

So: the **detection half**, landed for real. Reused `find_full_detail_overlaps` (the pure geometry function 235c787c already shipped and tested) rather than writing new code — a VWD REFR's cell is the same "still-resident full-detail thing that must not sit inside a LOD quad's footprint" shape the function already answers for `state.loaded`, just gathered from a different live source (`resident_vwd_refr_cells` in `streaming_helpers.rs`). Feeds a new `vwd_full_model_overlaps` field into the existing `LodCoverageStats` resource — `verdict()`/`machine_line()`/`lod.coverage` all picked it up for free.

Reads 0 on every real session today, which is the point: it proves the ring-separation argument holds on live traversals, not just by the construction proof, and becomes the actual regression gate for the day anyone does the radius decoupling. Wired into `m-exteriors.sh`'s existing `lod.coverage` hard gate. `cargo test -q` clean across both touched crates (`byroredux-core` 650/650, `byroredux` 1323/1323); full workspace run has one failure entirely outside this change, in the concurrent water-subsystem work landing throughout this session — reproduces on an unmodified `byroredux-renderer` tree.

## Still open on this issue

- **The active VWD cull itself** — needs the radius decoupling described above plus real-game visual validation; deliberately not attempted this session.
- **Near-cell crack/discontinuity detection** — the issue's own problem statement still has no gate for full-detail LAND tile seams (a different geometry class than the LOD-ring/VWD audits so far).
- **Real-data LAND guards** — height/normal/vertex-color/splat/holes/collider-render agreement per game.
- **Cross-game calibration** — Oblivion Tamriel, FNV WastelandNV, Skyrim Tamriel, FO4 Commonwealth.

Implementation plan added in 5f1367f3: [exterior-readiness-plan.md, Tranche C § EX-10/11](https://github.com/matiaszanolli/ByroRedux/blob/main/docs/engine/exterior-readiness-plan.md#ex-1011-2371--near-terrain-correctness-and-distant-lod-bands). Not closing — this is a plan for review, no implementation yet.

Headline finding: the plan doc and ROADMAP.md's M35 row were themselves stale — substantial EX-11 work already landed 2026-08-12 through 08-19 (4/8/16/32 LOD band ladder, far-plane sizing + depth-resolution measurement, Skyrim .btr normal maps, a live overlap/churn audit gate) that neither doc reflected. Corrected both. Remaining real work: LAND real-data guards, adjacent-cell crack detection, extending the LOD coverage gate to catch near-field geometry issues. VWD active culling and reversed-Z are scoped out as their own follow-up issues given their blast radius (the ring-separation argument already prevents the correctness issue VWD culling would fix; reversed-Z touches 6+ renderer subsystems).

**EX-10/11 item 5 (LAND real-data guards) — partially re-scoped, done what's buildable** (commit `b4a6c9ea`).

Investigating this surfaced that half its premise was already wrong: BTXT/ATXT FormID existence is already checked at consume time (`spawn_terrain_mesh` warns + skips a layer whose LTEX doesn't resolve) — not a parse-time gap. The other half (height/VNML/VCLR value-plausibility bounds) needs real corpus-derived thresholds to avoid guessing, and no game data was available this session to derive them, so that stays open.

What landed: the missing `land.rs` test file for `parse_land_record` — 9 tests covering the VHGT delta-decode algorithm (including a forward-row-accumulation case that's the actual algorithmic risk in that function), VNML/VCLR storage, and the ATXT/VTXT layer-pairing contract. No such coverage existed before.

Next up on this issue: item 6 (adjacent-cell crack detection), which item 7 depends on.

**EX-10/11 item 6 (adjacent-cell crack detection) — pure checker done, live wiring flagged** (commit `a03e55d6`).

Landed `cell_loader::terrain_seam::check_seam`: a pure function comparing two adjacent cells' shared-edge heights + VNML bytes, reporting facts rather than inventing a pass/fail tolerance (no real corpus data to calibrate one against — same constraint item 5 hit). 8 unit tests.

Item 7's prerequisite for wiring this live into `m-exteriors.sh` turns out to be bigger than "add a check": `LandscapeData` isn't retained anywhere after `spawn_terrain_mesh` runs today (it's a transient parse-result). Flagged the two design options in the plan doc (full-grid retention vs. edge-only cache) rather than picking one without more thought.

With EX-10/11's remaining items either deliberately deferred (8, 9 — already flagged as their own follow-up issues) or gated on live-wiring work I've now scoped but not built, I'm moving to EX-14/15 (#2369) next — starting with the persistent-ref cross-worldspace continuity thread (item C2), which is unblocked and well-scoped.
